events.title: Lady Jane Grey is executed
events.description: Lady Jane Grey was beheaded at the Tower of London. She was 16 or 17. She had been proclaimed queen of England for just nine days in 1553, before Mary I deposed her.
events.significance: Her fate shows how dangerous Tudor succession struggles were. It also shows how religion and politics shaped who held the English crown.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln and Charles Darwin are born
events.description: Two figures who would change the modern world were born on the same day. Abraham Lincoln was born in a Kentucky log cabin. Charles Darwin was born in Shrewsbury, England.
events.significance: Lincoln led the United States through the Civil War and the end of slavery. Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection transformed biology.

events.title: The NAACP is founded
events.description: On the centennial of Lincoln's birth, a group of activists founded the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People in the United States.
events.significance: It became one of America's most influential civil rights organizations. It spent the following decades fighting segregation and discrimination through the courts and public campaigns.

events.title: China's last emperor abdicates
events.description: Six-year-old Puyi, the Xuantong Emperor, abdicated the throne. This ended the Qing dynasty.
events.significance: The abdication ended more than two thousand years of imperial rule in China and opened the way for the Republic of China.

events.title: President Clinton is acquitted by the Senate
events.description: The U.S. Senate voted to acquit Bill Clinton on both articles of impeachment. The House of Representatives had impeached him in December 1998.
events.significance: Clinton was only the second U.S. president to be impeached. He remained in office and served out his term.
